why: The answer writes the right plan, copying data2 into copy one element at a time in a for loop. It has two mistakes: the bound i <= data2.length goes one index too far and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at i == data2.length, and copy is never created with new int[data2.length]. New code must be correct to reach L4, so this is L2 with an error.

concepts.why: int is used correctly as the type of the loop index, but no int rule is reasoned about.

data2.length is correctly written as a field with no parentheses, but using <= instead of < reaches index data2.length, one past the last valid index data2.length-1. That counts as a slip in the bound, not a stated wrong rule.
The init, test and update are well formed, but the test gives one pass too many (a wrong iteration count), so the last pass reads outside the array.
i++ is used correctly as the update that adds 1 to the index after each pass.
It copies element by element, which is right, but it never creates the new array copy and it runs past the end of data2, so the code fails.
The answer avoids copy = data2 but says nothing about aliasing.
